title: 语言模型能力评测的技术演进
content_md: # 语言模型能力评测的技术演进：机制、比较与边界 ## 摘要 本文全面回顾了语言模型能力评测方法从单一宏观指标到深层机制探测的演进历程。早期综合基准因快速饱和暴露出与模型真实能力的脱节，促使评测转向零样本或少样本设定以精准衡量预训练阶段的知识获取。随着模型规模的扩张与应用场景的泛化，评测重心由显式知识记忆转向复杂的结构化推理、全域安全性考量及人机交互验证。基准的构建也从扁平化的数据集堆砌，稳步升级为能力分类导向的层次化框架。此外，现代评测不断向低资源、多语言外推及深层语义探测延伸，通过引入心理语言学诊断及受控探测技术，揭示了模型在长程依赖规律、逻辑鲁棒性及机制盲区上的深层脆弱。整体而言，当前模型度量正迈向更精细、多维且兼顾认知与安全对齐的综合体系。 ## 研究问题与技术前史 语言模型能力评测的研究问题经历了从追求综合榜单分数到深入探究预训练机制与复杂推理能力的演变。早期自然语言理解基准（如GLUE和SuperGLUE）在发布后约一年内即被顶级模型达到人类水平，这种快速饱和暴露了基准分数与模型实际语言理解全貌之间的脱节[9]。为更准确衡量模型在预训练阶段获取的世界知识，评测方法转向纯零样本和少样本设置，利用涵盖数十个学科的大规模多任务框架进行测试；结果表明，尽管最大参数的GPT-3模型相较随机猜测平均提升了近20个百分点，但距离专家级准确率仍需大幅改进[9]。 随着模型规模扩大，研究重心逐渐从显式知识提取转向复杂结构化推理。尽管有观点认为扩展规模即可全面隐式编码常识，但评测表明，先进神经模型在表达涉及复杂关系的隐式常识时依然面临困难[7]。例如在少样本设定下，175B参数的GPT-3模型的表现比在特定常识图谱上训练的小模型仍低约12个绝对百分点[7]。同时，针对模型“推理”能力的评测也迎来了方法论的反思。早期推理基准被批评过于简单，无法支撑关于模型具备真实推理能力的夸大主张[49]。由于语言模型本质上提供最可能的文本补全而缺乏逻辑保证，研究者引入目标导向的确定性规划框架，以测量模型在行动与状态变化上的真实边界[49]。在算法推理等需要多步生成的场景中，单次生成的成功率随代码模块增加呈指数级下降，这也促使评测框架引入自然语言分层约束，以测试模型在组合验证空间下的代码合成能力[48]。 在多语言与语言学特征演进方面，早期依赖机器翻译英语基准来构建多语言评测的做法，暴露出引入翻译伪影及无法捕捉特定社会文化特征的缺陷，促使了基于原生语料从头构建基准的转向[21]。对于具丰富形态句法的语言，传统语义测试亦显不足。层级探测（probing）分支研究发现，高度多语言模型能在中间网络层定位句法知识，而部分专注特定语系训练的模型却未能有效捕获此类句法特征[25]。从宏观任务精度到微观神经表示的演进，构成了当前大模型度量技术的重要前史。 ## 评价对象、威胁模型与测量 语言模型能力评测的演进深刻反映了其底层机制与应用场景的变迁。在评价对象的早期阶段，模型评测主要关注特定应用中的领域适应能力。当时的测量机制侧重于应对训练与测试数据之间的分布不匹配（domain mismatch）以及由罕见词导致的数据稀疏性问题，往往通过结合自动数据选择与循环神经网络语言模型（RNNLM）的特征来提升泛化性能，其评估高度依赖于特定领域的统计测度[3]。 随着大型语言模型被应用于大规模代码合成等复杂推理任务，评价对象从单纯的文本概率预测转向对高阶规范和复杂逻辑执行能力的综合考量。这一转变直接催生了多维度的威胁模型框架。针对以Codex为代表的代码生成模型，早期的危险分析不仅审视其生成能力，更强调其在处理无正式规范和不可靠训练数据时的局限性[27]。在具体的测量机制上，此类框架深入探究了模型能力的边界。例如，尽管模型能够处理少量变量的关联，但当提示词中涉及四个或更多变量的相互依赖关系时，若相关逻辑未在训练数据中高频出现，Codex等模型的推理能力便会发生显著衰退[27]。为了应对这种深层逻辑隐患，威胁模型甚至向底层机制延伸，建议将模型的API输出直接与编程语言的抽象语法树（AST）对齐，以更稳健地适配现有的安全审计探测机制[27]。 在代码生成领域，相较于单纯验证模型自身输出的静态分析（即“自动驾驶”模式），现代测量机制逐步分化出以人类开发者真实交互为核心的实证评估分支。针对大模型可能直接建议网络安全漏洞的担忧，基于用户对照研究的动态测量机制提供了有别于基准刷榜的视角。通过在内存安全缺陷极易触发的底层语言（如C语言）环境中设置链表开发任务，实验测量表明，引入大模型辅助开发并不会直接引发显著的安全危机——模型辅助组产生严重安全漏洞的比例相比无辅助控制组增幅不超过10%[52]。然而，这种结合用户行为的测量方式也揭示了隐蔽的交互性风险：开发者常常利用AI模型带来的生产力提升来加速编码，却未能有效识别并修复模型建议中本身夹带的代码缺陷；即使他们对建议代码的变量名等进行了微调，底层的逻辑漏洞依然被无意识地保留并部署[52]。 此外，广义的威胁模型与评测对象已经突破了代码能否安全执行的单一维度，开始拓展至知识归属与合规性边界的探测。研究指出，模型生成的代码在解决常规编程问题时，能够有效绕过诸如MOSS等传统代码反抄袭软件的检测[52]。这一现象不仅揭示了评测机制面临的新挑战，也进一步证明了对语言模型能力的评价必须从早期的统计精度测量，走向涵盖人机信任、逻辑边界探测以及交互安全性的全域综合验证。 ## 基准构建、检测与防护 语言模型能力评测的演进不仅体现在任务难度的增加，更核心的在于基准构建机制的结构性转变。早期阶段的语言模型评估往往采用扁平化（Flat）的数据集导向框架，即将常用数据集松散组合，并普遍依赖过度简化的评分策略——直接对跨数据集的独立指标进行简单平均。这种机制严重忽略了不同自然语言处理任务间的异质性与度量差异，导致最终的单一均分无法准确反映模型在特定语言能力层面（如推理或生成）的真实优劣，破坏了基准作为通用语言智能指示器的可靠性。 为解决上述系统性缺失，现代基准构建机制开始向自顶向下的层次化（Hierarchical）框架发生范式转移。以中文语言理解与生成评测基准CUGE为例，其摒弃了传统的底层数据堆砌模式，创新性地构建了“能力-任务-数据集”的三级分类体系[19]。在这种机制下，基准设计参考人类语言考试大纲，将通用语言智能预先解构为篇章级理解、信息获取与问答、多语言及数学推理等七大核心能力，随后再向下映射至代表性任务和具体数据集。这种结构化设计的核心优势在于其支持多级评分策略（Multi-level scoring strategy），使得研究者能够基于层次框架输出不同细粒度的模型性能评估结果，从而精细化定位语言模型在特定能力层级的真实表现与提升空间[19]。 在通用自然语言基准之外，面向特定下游模态的语言模型评测则展现出差异化的机制侧重点。尤其是在自动语音识别（ASR）领域，语言模型的评测焦点从静态文本的完形填空，显著转向对动态、长跨度词史（word history）信息的连续映射能力评估。例如，在针对递回式神经网络语言模型（RNNLM）的评测中，研究者通常以大词汇量连续语音识别（LVCSR）任务作为核心的实证检验基准[2]。在该特定任务基准下，评测机制重点考察模型在结合词史相关额外信息线索时，通过递归方式捕获长距离词汇规律的有效性，以及利用动态模型估计方法获取特定话语（utterance-specific）特征的性能表现[2]。这种依托LVCSR任务开展的纵深对比评测，构成了对通用层次化基准不可或缺的专业补充。 需要特别指出的是，全面而可靠的语言模型评测应当涵盖对恶意注入、数据投毒等威胁的检测与防护机制。然而，基于严谨的文献适用范围，当前有效材料集中于基础评测框架的架构演进与特定任务的性能检验，尚未涵盖针对语言模型幻觉甄别、对抗鲁棒性检测或对齐防护策略的具体技术论证。因此，关于安全检测与防护维度的机制探讨予以明确限定，暂不涉及相关无证据主张。 ## 有效性、鲁棒性和外推边界 语言模型能力的评测正逐步从常规的同分布任务，向低资源场景、复杂语义现象等边缘地带延伸，以全面探究模型的有效性、鲁棒性及其外推边界。在评测方法的分支演进中，针对跨分布和隐含语义偏移的测量机制尤为关键。 在鲁棒性与外推边界的评测分支中，多语言及语码交替（Code-Switching）场景构成了重要的测试床。传统的语言模型在面对多语言混合输入时，常受限于真实混合数据的稀缺以及语言间语法结构的错位。为了探明模型在此类数据不平衡条件下的外推能力，研究者改变了直接依赖真实数据的评测范式。例如，基于等价约束（Equivalence Constraint）理论，通过形态素分割与词对齐技术，人工合成合乎语法的混合语言文本进行模型增强与评估[36]。这种机制转变允许在无额外真实混合语音数据的条件下，验证语言模型处理复杂输入形态的鲁棒性。在有效性测量上，此类方法不仅通过困惑度（如实现29-34%的相对增益）等客观指标来量化模型的边界扩展，还结合人类主观判断评估生成数据与真实生态数据的接近度，以此确立外推分布的可靠性[36]。 在语义理解的有效性探测分支中，模型处理选择性限制（Selectional Restrictions）违背现象（如逻辑转喻中的论元强制）的能力是评估其语义推理边界的核心指标。传统方法在无监督地捕捉这种隐含意图时面临挑战。为了评测和提升模型对论元强制（Argument Coercion）的检测能力，评测机制演进为通过无监督主题模型（如带有谓词归纳和选择类变量的cLDA）来进行概率推断[1]。与依赖单一显式特征不同，该机制利用谓词-类别与论元-类别的概率混合，对谓词-论元对进行连续区间打分（低分指向强制现象），从而在不依赖标注数据的情况下，评估模型识别非标准语义搭配的有效性[1]。这种基于数据分布采样的打分机制，揭示了模型在面对单义常见谓词与多义词汇时，无监督语义归纳能力的边界差异。 综上，针对模型有效性和鲁棒性的评测，正从单一的性能跑分转向对模型内在机制的深层探测。无论是通过语法理论约束生成跨语言外推数据，还是利用无监督概率模型检测深层语义违背现象，这些演进机制均极大地丰富了对语言模型在极端或复杂约束下能力边界的认知。 ## 实验证据与方法比较 语言模型评测逐渐暴露出现有指标的局限与冲突。传统的困惑度和全局准确率极易受齐夫分布影响，导致低频词惩罚，掩盖模型在开放域生成中的实际语义可用性[6][22]。然而，当训练数据限定在人类发展合理规模时，困惑度能有效反映模型与人类神经行为的对齐程度[29]，甚至可作为下游代码任务的低成本评估代理[28]。为避免复杂任务军备竞赛，评估演进出针对琐碎任务的自动单元测试[44]；早期依赖单一语料规模的基准[4]开始向细粒度对照诊断转型。 评测范式从端到端打分转向施加严密的对照条件。结构知识检验利用最小对立体探测局部约束与C-统御[5]，将心理语言学实验平台化以验证句法机制[12]，或通过句法启动效应分离语义与抽象结构表征[23]。评测还通过疑问化反事实条件句限制推理捷径[18]，系统隔离36类语言现象以暴露推断缺陷[38]。在约束生成方面，评估引入基于正则表达式状态机的大规模形式化验证[57]，以及利用上下文无关文法限制解码空间的语义解析测试[31]。针对纯文本分布伪影，评测扩展至棋类等闭域环境，利用完整状态追踪机制消除不可观测干扰[26]；代码理解中则通过对齐抽象语法树的注意力权重，暴露了模型不及位置偏移基线的结构弱点[32]。 任务构建呈现难度分级与语言类型学分化。生成任务被拆分为多级难度以量化泛化边界[8]。多语言评测从早期从头构建原生语料基准[11]、防过拟合未公开数据校验[56]及专属生成框架[30]，向深层特性扩展：如西班牙语评估涵盖了基于语篇连贯的序列特征[42]。类型学测试揭示了深层差异：日语测试暴露出模型对语序和格助词极不敏感[37]；英西对比表明模型的句法偏好往往源于非语言近因偏差，而非通用规律[10]。此外，基于类型学特征的预测机制能替代翻译，更无偏地估计零样本迁移[34]；中低资源场景下单语定制模型常优于大规模多语言架构[17]，但在特定推理中，高资源语言思维链中间步骤却能反向提升低资源语言解题率[45]。研究还通过声形感知嵌入探测正字法差异[43]，利用伪概率评估无监督语音建模[13]，而跨文化评测更揭示了摆脱西方中心化偏见的深刻挑战[59]。 实验揭示了架构在各类场景下的机制盲点与脆弱性。零样本泛化中，自回归因果解码器表现最佳，但掩码模型结合多任务微调亦能在特定对齐下反超[58]；常识评测表明零样本的高性能往往源于数据集偏差[14]，但大规模模型在物理属性判断中却展现出克服局部共现报告偏差的能力[39]。指令微调无法填补模型在语用学会话含义推理上的鸿沟[54]；定向微调虽能唤醒被掩盖的隐式语言知识[24]，但在事实一致性评测中，解码器依旧优先给违背事实但字面摘抄文本打高分[41]。代码漏洞修复成功率极度依赖提示注释的句法分布[20]。句法保持替换[40]与对抗性拼写微扰[15]分别暴露出模型在维持语言结构稳定性和保持语义鲁棒性方面的深层缺陷。对话问答中，将历史线索直接作为文本提示注入比修改特征表征更具鲁棒性[47]；困难推理任务中，仅依赖答案评分会严重低估能力，必须结合思维链反映真实计算边界[35]。最后，语音理解应用中，紧凑模型在维持可比错误率的同时显著降低了部署生态影响，但这取决于具体的压缩方法，且特定模型效果甚至优于蒸馏版本[33]。 ## 局限、效率与开放问题 尽管语言模型在各项基准上取得了显著成绩，但现有的评测方法在适用条件、测量有效性及部署成本上仍面临严峻局限。首先，在评测指标的有效性与泛化边界检测方面，基础指标与实际能力之间存在机制性脱节。验证集的预训练损失（如困惑度）无法完全解释模型在下游任务中的表现差异；研究发现，即使预训练损失相同，不同参数配置的模型也会因优化算法（如带小批量噪声的随机梯度下降）对平缓极小值的隐式偏好，而导致下游任务的迁移能力大相径庭[51]。同时，由于模型倾向于拟合容易学习的表层文本相关性而非深层语义逻辑，其在分布外（OOD）数据上的鲁棒性往往大幅下降[46]。这引发了研究界对模型是否真正具备“理解”能力的争议：许多自然语言理解基准（如GLUE）的高分表现，可能仅仅是模型利用了数据的脆弱启发式特征，而非实现了类似人类的认知推理[55]。为了在无标注目标域数据时估计这种分布偏移，虽然引入了基于隐层属性的无监督泛化度量，但其与实际分布外准确率的等级相关性依然受限[46]。 其次，在特定维度的风险测量机制上，当前方法表现出极大的脆弱性。以社会偏见量化为例，广泛使用的模板化填空评测机制极不可靠；在保持语义不变的前提下对模板进行人工微调，会导致特定任务（如自然语言推断或掩码语言建模）的偏见测量结果发生剧烈波动，这种不稳定性证明单一静态模板难以真实反映模型的复杂行为模式，容易产生误导性结论[50]。 最后，评测体系的适用边界还受到计算成本与语言多样性的制约。大规模语言模型的极高计算开销严重限制了其推理部署，促使研究转向渐进式非结构化幅度剪枝等压缩技术，以在仅保留约十分之一参数量的条件下，维持通用模型在特定（如生物医学）领域的跨域迁移质量[53]。此外，在多语言评测场景中，通用的统一文本框架（如mT5）在面对具有丰富方言变体和复杂形态的低资源语言时，其跨语言迁移能力存在明显瓶颈；针对特定语言族群进行专门的序列预训练（如AraT5），成为突破通用架构能力盲区、触及生成与理解评测上限的必要条件[16]。 ## 结论 语言模型评测的不断演进，深刻反映了人工智能技术向真实复杂场景落地的挑战。尽管先进大模型在常规榜单上已达人类水平，但针对细粒度内部机制、因果推理及类型学的针对性探测表明，其在维持句法稳定、克服局部统计偏差、防御交互式风险等维度依然存在根本性局限。现代评估体系通过引入形式化约束生成、心理语言学平台化验证与严密的动态用户对照，有效避免了单一平均分引发的误导性结论。未来的评测发展应进一步剥离西方中心化偏见与数据分布伪影，在权衡计算部署成本与生态影响的前提下，建立具备更强因果解释力及跨文化泛化性的验证标准，从而为新一代语言智能的可靠性提供坚实保障。 ## source_intervals.text: Recurrent neural network-based language modeling with extra information cues for speech recognition The goal of language modeling (LM) attempts to capture the regularities of natural languages. It uses large amounts of training text for model training so as to help predict the most likely upcoming word given a word history. Therefore, it plays an indispensable role in automatic speech recognition (ASR). The N-gram language model, which determines the probability of an upcoming word given its preceding N-1 word history, is most prominently used. When N is small, a typical N-gram language model lacks the ability of rendering long-span lexical information. On the other hand, when N becomes larger, it will suffer from the data sparseness problem because of insufficient training data. With this acknowledged, research on the neural network-based language model (NNLM), or more specifically, the feed-forward NNLM, has attracted considerable attention of researchers and practitioners in recent years. This is attributed to the fact that the feed-forward NNLM can mitigate the data sparseness problem when estimating the probability of an upcoming word given its corresponding word history through mapping them into a continuous space. In addition to the feed-forward NNLM, a recent trend is to use the recurrent neural network-based language model (RNNLM) to construct the language model for AS

R, which can make efficient use of the long-span lexical information inherent in the word history in a recursive fashion. In this thesis, we not only investigate to leverage extra information relevant to the word history for RNNLM, but also devise a dynamic model estimation method

to obtain an utterance-specific RNNLM. We experimentally observe that our proposed methods can show promise and perform well when compared to the existing LM methods on a large vocabulary continuous speech recognition (LVCSR) task.

In this paper, we, benefit from salient performance of recurrent neural network to improve domain adapted LM. In this way, we first apply an automatic data selection procedure on a limited amount of in-domain data in order to enrich the training set. source_intervals.text: One Billion Word Benchmark for Measuring Progress in Statistical Language Modeling We propose a new benchmark corpus to be used for measuring progress in statistical language modeling. With almost one billion words of training data, we hope this benchmark will be useful to quickly evaluate novel language modeling techniques, and to compare their contribution when combined with other advanced techniques. We show performance of several well-known types of language models, with the best results achieved with a recurrent neural network based language model. The baseline unpruned Kneser-Ney 5-gram model achieves perplexity 67.6; a combination of techniques leads to 35% reduction in perplexity, or 10% reduction in cross-entropy (bits), over that baseline. While this approach has shown NLMs to be capable of learning a wide range of linguistic knowledge, confounds in the design of previous experiments may have obscured the potential of NLMs to learn certain grammatical phenomena. A question of interest to both the NLP and cognitive science communities is what generalizations neural models are able to implicitly acquire while optimizing performance on the language modeling task. source_intervals.text: Are Some Words Worth More than Others? Current evaluation metrics for language modeling and generation rely heavily on the accuracy of predicted (or generated) words as compared to a reference ground truth. While important, token-level accuracy only captures one aspect of a language model’s behavior, and ignores linguistic properties of words that may allow some mis-predicted tokens to be useful in practice. Furthermore, statistics directly tied to prediction accuracy (including perplexity) may be confounded by the Zipfian nature of written language, as the majority of the prediction attempts will occur with frequently-occurring types. A model’s performance may vary greatly between high- and low-frequency words, which in practice could lead to failure modes such as repetitive and dull generated text being produced by a downstream consumer of a language model. To address this, we propose two new intrinsic evaluation measures within the framework of a simple word prediction task that are designed to give a more holistic picture of a language model’s performance. We evaluate several commonly-used large English language models using our proposed metrics, and demonstrate that our approach reveals functional differences in performance between the models that are obscured by more traditional metrics. source_intervals.text: GLGE: A New General Language Generation Evaluation Benchmark Multi-task benchmarks such as GLUE and SuperGLUE have driven great progress of pretraining and transfer learning in Natural Language Processing (NLP). These benchmarks mostly focus on a range of Natural Language Understanding (NLU) tasks, without considering the Natural Language Generation (NLG) models. In this paper, we present the General Language Generation Evaluation (GLGE), a new multi-task benchmark for evaluating the generalization capabilities of NLG models across eight language generation tasks. For each task, we continue to design three subtasks in terms of task difficulty (GLGE-Easy, GLGE-Medium, and GLGE-Hard). This introduces 24 subtasks to comprehensively compare model performance. To encourage research on pretraining and transfer learning on NLG models, we make GLGE publicly available and build a leaderboard with strong baselines including MASS, BART, and ProphetNet (The source code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/microsoft/glge). To better understand the challenges posed by GLGE, we conduct experiments with existing widely used non-pretrained models (e.g., vanilla LSTM Seq2Seq

source_intervals.text: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding We propose a new test to measure a text model's multitask accuracy. The test covers 57 tasks including elementary mathematics, US history, computer science, law, and more. To attain high accuracy on this test, models must possess extensive world knowledge and problem solving ability. We find that while most recent models have near random-chance accuracy, the very largest GPT-3 model improves over random chance by almost 20 percentage points on average. However, on every one of the 57 tasks, the best models still need substantial improvements before they can reach expert-level accuracy. Models also have lopsided performance and frequently do not know when they are wrong. Worse, they still have near-random accuracy on some socially important subjects such as morality and law. By comprehensively evaluating the breadth and depth of a model's academic and professional understanding, our test can be used to analyze models across many tasks and to identify important shortcomings. We ask whether these models exhibit commonsense understanding – a critical component of NLP applications – by evaluating models against four commonsense benchmarks. We find that the impressive zeroshot performance of large language models is mostly due to existence of dataset bias in our benchmarks. Existing work has shown that non-linguistic biases in models can drive model behavior away from linguistic generalizations. We hypothesized that competing linguistic processes within a language, rather than just non-linguistic model biases, could obscure underlying linguistic knowledge. Our results suggest that models need to learn both the linguistic constraints in a language and their relative ranking, with mismatches in either producing non-human-like behavior. source_intervals.text: Vyākarana: A Colorless Green Benchmark for Syntactic Evaluation in Indic Languages While there has been significant progress towards developing NLU resources for Indic languages, syntactic evaluation has been relatively less explored. Unlike English, Indic languages have rich morphosyntax, grammatical genders, free linear word-order, and highly inflectional morphology. In this paper, we introduce Vyākarana: a benchmark of Colorless Green sentences in Indic languages for syntactic evaluation of multilingual language models. The benchmark comprises four syntax-related tasks: PoS Tagging, Syntax Tree-depth Prediction, Grammatical Case Marking, and Subject-Verb Agreement. We use the datasets from the evaluation tasks to probe five multilingual language models of varying architectures for syntax in Indic languages. Due to its prevalence, we also include a code-switching setting in our experiments. Our results show that the token-level and sentence-level representations from the Indic language models (IndicBERT and MuRIL) do not capture the syntax in Indic languages as efficiently as the other highly multilingual language models. Further, our layer-wise probing experiments reveal that while mBERT, DistilmBERT, and XLM-R localize the syntax in middle layers, the Indic language models do not show such syntactic localization. source_intervals.text: Artificial neural network language models align neurally and behaviorally with humans even after a developmentally realistic amount of training Artificial neural networks have emerged as computationally plausible models of human language processing. A major criticism of these models is that the amount of training data they receive far exceeds that of humans during language learning. Here, we use two complementary approaches to ask how the models’ ability to capture human neural and behavioral responses to language is affected by the amount of training data. First, we evaluate GPT-2 models trained on 1 million, 10 million, 100 million, or 1 billion tokens against two fMRI benchmarks and one behavioral (reading times) benchmark. Because children are exposed to approximately 100 million words during the first 10 years of life, we consider the 100-million-token model developmentally plausible. Second, we test the performance of a GPT-2 model that is trained on a 9-billion dataset to reach state-of-the-art next-word prediction performance against the same human benchmarks at different stages during training. Across both approaches, we find that (i) the models trained on a developmentally plausible amount of data already achieve near-maximal performance in capturing neural and behavioral responses to language. Further, (ii) lower perplexity—a measure of next-word prediction performan

ce—is associated with stronger alignment with the human benchmarks, suggesting that models that have received enough training to achieve sufficiently high next-word prediction performance also acquire human-like representations of the linguistic input. In tandem, these findings establish that although some training is necessary for the models’ ability to predict human responses to language,

a developmentally realistic amount of training (∼100 million tokens) may suffice. Summary Are artificial neural network (ANN) language models useful as models of human language processing? Some of these models have been shown to capture human responses to language with relatively high accuracy. However, these models are trained on vastly more data than what children are exposed to during language acquisition, raising questions about their value for understanding the human language system. Here, we systematically manipulate the amount of training data that ANN models receive and show that models that are trained on developmentally plausible amounts of language data (approximately 100 million words, roughly corresponding to a child’s first 10 years of life) achieve near-maximal performance on human neural and behavioral benchmarks. We aggregate three challenging conditional text generation tasks under the BanglaNLG benchmark. Then, using a clean corpus of 27.5 GB of Bangla data, we pretrain BanglaT5, a sequence-to-sequence Transformer model for Bangla. BanglaT5 achieves state-of-the-art performance in all of these tasks, outperforming mT5 (base) by up to 5.4%. source_intervals.text: BenchCLAMP: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Semantic Parsing We introduce BenchCLAMP, a Benchmark to evaluate Constrained LAnguage Model Parsing, which produces semantic outputs based on the analysis of input text through constrained decoding of a prompted or fine-tuned language model. Developers of pretrained language models currently benchmark on classification, span extraction and free-text generation tasks. Semantic parsing is neglected in language model evaluation because of the complexity of handling task-specific architectures and representations. Recent work has shown that generation from a prompted or fine-tuned language model can perform well at semantic parsing when the output is constrained to be a valid semantic representation. BenchCLAMP includes context-free grammars for six semantic parsing datasets with varied output meaning representations, as well as a constrained decoding interface to generate outputs covered by these grammars. We provide low, medium, and high resource splits for each dataset, allowing accurate comparison of various language models under different data regimes. Our benchmark supports both prompt-based learning as well as fine-tuning, and provides an easy-to-use toolkit for language model developers to evaluate on semantic parsing. Although these approaches are increasingly popular, they require large amounts of data and computational resources. There is still a substantial need for benchmarking methodologies ever upwards on under-resourced languages in data-scarce application conditions. Most pre-trained language models were massively studied using the English language and only a few of them were evaluated on French. But on what tasks do language models fall short of average human-rater performance, and are those tasks actually unsolvable by current language models? Since many tasks in BBH require multi-step reasoning, few-shot prompting without CoT, as done in the BIG-Bench evaluations (Srivastava et al., 2022), substantially underestimates the best performance and capabilities of language models, which is better captured via CoT prompting. source_intervals.text: Code-Switching Text Augmentation for Multilingual Speech Processing The pervasiveness of intra-utterance Code-switching (CS) in spoken content has enforced ASR systems to handle mixed input. Yet, designing a CS-ASR has many challenges, mainly due to the data scarcity, grammatical structure complexity, and mismatch along with unbalanced language usage distribution. Recent ASR studies showed the predominance of E2E-ASR using multilingual data to handle CS phenomena with little CS data. However, the dependency on the CS data still remains. In this work, we propose a methodology to augment the monolingual data for artificially generating spoken CS text to improve different speech modules. We based our approach on Equivalence Constraint theory while exploiting aligned translation pairs, to generate grammatically valid CS content. Our empirical results show a relative gain of 29-34 % in perplexity and around 2% in WER for two ecological and noisy CS test sets. Finally, the human evaluation suggests that 83.8% of the generated data is acceptable to humans. INTRODUCTION Code-switching (CS) is a prevalent phenomenon in multi-cultural and multi-lingual society due to the advent of globalization and also as a result of colonization. Code-switching is a phenomena, where speakers alter between two or more languages during the spoken discourse, has attracted the attention of speech researche

On the other hand, [13] proposed to model the CS with a sequence to sequence recurrent neural network (RNN) with attention, that learns when to switch and copy words from parallel sentences. However, this approach still requires having considerable amount of CS data for adaptation. In this work, we propose to generate CS data based on EC theory. First, we build parallel data by translating original Arabic content into

source_intervals.text: Compositional Evaluation on Japanese Textual Entailment and Similarity Natural Language Inference (NLI) and Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) are widely used benchmark tasks for compositional evaluation of pre-trained language models. Despite growing interest in linguistic universals, most NLI/STS studies have focused almost exclusively on English. In particular, there are no available multilingual NLI/STS datasets in Japanese, which is typologically different from English and can shed light on the currently controversial behavior of language models in matters such as sensitivity to word order and case particles. Against this background, we introduce JSICK, a Japanese NLI/STS dataset that was manually translated from the English dataset SICK. We also present a stress-test dataset for compositional inference, created by transforming syntactic structures of sentences in JSICK to investigate whether language models are sensitive to word order and case particles. We conduct baseline experiments on different pre-trained language models and compare the performance of multilingual models when applied to Japanese and other languages. The results of the stress-test experiments suggest that the current pre-trained language models are insensitive to word order and case marking. Experiments showed that BERT performance for Japanese is consistently worse than that for Indo-European languages. source_intervals.text: Evaluating the Factual Consistency of Large Language Models Through Summarization While large language models (LLMs) have proven to be effective on a large variety of tasks, they are also known to hallucinate information. To measure whether an LLM prefers factually consistent continuations of its input, we propose a new benchmark called FIB(Factual Inconsistency Benchmark) that focuses on the task of summarization. Specifically, our benchmark involves comparing the scores an LLM assigns to a factually consistent versus a factually inconsistent summary for an input news article. For factually consistent summaries, we use human-written reference summaries that we manually verify as factually consistent. To generate summaries that are factually inconsistent, we generate summaries from a suite of summarization models that we have manually annotated as factually inconsistent. A model's factual consistency is then measured according to its accuracy, i.e.\ the proportion of documents where it assigns a higher score to the factually consistent summary. To validate the usefulness of FIB, we evaluate 23 large language models ranging from 1B to 176B parameters from six different model families including BLOOM and OPT. While existing models show impressive results on CQA leaderboards, it remains unclear whether they are robust to shifts in setting (sometimes to more realistic ones), training data size (e.g. from large to small sets) and domain. In this work, we design and conduct the first large-scale robustness study of history modeling approaches for CQA. We find that high benchmark scores do not necessarily translate to strong robustness, and that various methods can perform extremely differently under different settings. Equipped with the insights from our study, we design a novel prompt-based history modeling approach, and demonstrate its strong robustness across various settings. Our approach is inspired by existing methods that highlight historic answers in the passage. However, instead of highlighting by modifying the passage token embeddings, we add textual prompts directly in the passage text. Our approach is simple, easy-to-plug into practically any model, and highly effective, thus we recommend it as a starting point for future model developers. The validation pre-training loss (or perplexity in autoregressive language modeling) is often used as the evaluation metric when developing language models since the pre-training loss tends to be well-correlated with downstream performance (which is itself difficult to evaluate comprehensively). On simplified datasets, we identify three ways to produce models with the same (statistically optimal) pre-training loss but different downstream performance: continue pre-training after convergence, increasing the model size, and changing the training algorithm. These experiments demonstrate the existence of implicit bias of pre-training algorithms/optimizers -- among models with the same minimal pre-training loss, they implicitly prefer more transferable ones. source_intervals.text: Security Implications of Large Language Model Code Assistants: A User Study Large Language Models (LLMs) such as OpenAI Codex are increasingly being used as AI-based coding assistants. Understanding the impact of these tools on developers' code is paramount, especially as recent work showed that LLMs may suggest cybersecurity vulnerabilities. We conduct a security-driven user study (N=58) to assess code written by student programmers when assisted by LLMs. Given the potential severity of low-level bugs as well as their relative frequency in real-world projects, we tasked participants with implementing a singly-linked 'shopping list' structure in C. Our results indicate that the security impact in this setting is small: AI-assisted users produce critical security bugs at a rate no greater than 10% more than the control, indicating the use of LLMs does not introduce new security risks. Introduction Large Language Models (LLMs) are deep neural networks trained on massive text corpora [1,2] to learn the underlying distribution of natural language or structured text. When trained on code, LLMs can be used for code completion, bug fixing, and summarization [3][4][5], useful features for developers. Recent offerings are thus commercializing LLMs for code, including GitHub Copilot, which after its public release in June 2022 added 400,000 new users in just two months [6]. However, rece

Conclusions In this paper we set out to investigate the cybersecurity impact of LLM code suggestions on participants writing code in a user study. With N=58 users, we determined that the LLM has a likely beneficial impact on functional correctness; and does not increase the incidence rates of severe security bugs in our context. This is somewhat surprising given the existing published studies on how vulnerable code can be suggested by the models [7,8]. When considering the origin of bugs that were found, the data suggests that the users do not use the extra productivity benefits to fix bugs in their code-although suggestions are being modified (e.g. variable names), if a suggestion contained a bug it may not be fixed. source_intervals.text: Sparse*BERT: Sparse Models are Robust Large Language Models have become the core architecture upon which most modern natural language processing (NLP) systems build. These models can consistently deliver impressive accuracy and robustness across tasks and domains, but their high computational overhead can make inference difficult and expensive. To make the usage of these models less costly recent work has explored leveraging structured and unstructured pruning, quantization, and distillation as ways to improve inference speed and decrease size. This paper studies how models pruned using Gradual Unstructured Magnitude Pruning can transfer between domains and tasks. Our experimentation shows that models that are pruned during pretraining using general domain masked language models can transfer to novel domains and tasks without extensive hyperparameter exploration or specialized approaches. We demonstrate that our general sparse model Sparse*BERT can become SparseBioBERT simply by pretraining the compressed architecture on unstructured biomedical text. Moreover, we show that SparseBioBERT can match the quality of BioBERT with only 10\% of the parameters. source_intervals.text: Large language models are not zero-shot communicators Despite widespread use of LLMs as conversational agents, evaluations of performance fail to capture a crucial aspect of communication: interpreting language in context. Humans interpret language using beliefs and prior knowledge about the world. For example, we intuitively understand the response"I wore gloves"to the question"Did you leave fingerprints?"as meaning"No". To investigate whether LLMs have the ability to make this type of inference, known as an implicature, we design a simple task and evaluate widely used state-of-the-art models. We find that, despite only evaluating on utterances that require a binary inference (yes or no), most perform close to random. Models adapted to be"aligned with human intent"perform much better, but still show a significant gap with human performance. We present our findings as the starting point for further research into evaluating how LLMs interpret language in context and to drive the development of more pragmatic and useful models of human discourse. Conclusions and Future Work In this paper, we have introduced LEPISZCZE , a new comprehensive benchmark for Polish NLP. LEPISZCZE is characterized by the large variety of NLP tasks and high-quality operationalization of the benchmark. The benchmarking approach is designed to maximize the flexibility and portability of other low-resourced languages. Adding new models, datasets, or NLP tasks is simple and intuitive. source_intervals.text: Validating Large Language Models with ReLM Although large language models (LLMs) have been touted for their ability to generate natural-sounding text, there are growing concerns around possible negative effects of LLMs such as data memorization, bias, and inappropriate language. Unfortunately, the complexity and generation capacities of LLMs make validating (and correcting) such concerns difficult. In this work, we introduce ReLM, a system for validating and querying LLMs using standard regular expressions. ReLM formalizes and enables a broad range of language model evaluations, reducing complex evaluation rules to simple regular expression queries. Our results exploring queries surrounding memorization, gender bias, toxicity, and language understanding show that ReLM achieves up to 15x higher system efficiency, 2.5x data efficiency, and increased statistical and prompt-tuning coverage compared to state-of-the-art ad-hoc queries. ReLM offers a competitive and general baseline for the increasingly important problem of LLM validation. ReLM presents a convincing case against ad-hoc large language model validation, paving the way towards a programming abstraction that can increase researchers and practitioners' understanding of these complex models. source_intervals.text: What Language Model Architecture and Pretraining Objective Work Best for Zero-Shot Generalization? Large pretrained Transformer language models have been shown to exhibit zero-shot generalization, i.e. they can perform a wide variety of tasks that they were not explicitly trained on. However, the architectures and pretraining objectives used across state-of-the-art models differ significantly, and there has been limited systematic comparison of these factors. In this work, we present a large-scale evaluation of modeling choices and their impact on zero-shot generalization. In particular, we focus on text-to-text models and experiment with three model architectures (causal/non-causal decoder-only and encoder-decoder), trained with two different pretraining objectives (autoregressive and masked language modeling), and evaluated with and without multitask prompted finetuning. We train models with over 5 billion parameters for more than 170 billion tokens, thereby increasing the likelihood that our conclusions will transfer to even larger scales. source_intervals.text: You reap what you sow: On the Challenges of Bias Evaluation Under Multilingual Settings Evaluating bias, fairness, and social impact in monolingual language models is a difficult task. This challenge is further compounded when language modeling occurs in a multilingual context. Considering the implication of evaluation biases for large multilingual language models, we situate the discussion of bias evaluation within a wider context of social scientific research with computational work.We highlight three dimensions of developing multilingual bias evaluation frameworks: (1) increasing transparency through documentation, (2) expanding targets of bias beyond gender, and (3) addressing cultural differences that exist between languages.We further discuss the power dynamics and consequences of training large language models and recommend that researchers remain cognizant of the ramifications of developing such technologies. Introduction Machine learning (ML) systems, especially large language models (LLMs), are prone to (re)produce harmful outcomes and social biases (Bender et al., 2021;Raji et al., 2021;Blodgett et al., 2020;Aguera y Arcas et al., 2018). Conclusion Recent improvements in LLMs to mimic human text have led to a surge in research that seeks to identify and address the harms arising from their training and deployment. sections.title: 研究问题与技术前史
sections.body:
语言模型能力评测的研究问题经历了从追求综合榜单分数到深入探究预训练机制与复杂推理能力的演变。早期自然语言理解基准（如GLUE和SuperGLUE）在发布后约一年内即被顶级模型达到人类水平，这种快速饱和暴露了基准分数与模型实际语言理解全貌之间的脱节[9]。为更准确衡量模型在预训练阶段获取的世界知识，评测方法转向纯零样本和少样本设置，利用涵盖数十个学科的大规模多任务框架进行测试；结果表明，尽管最大参数的GPT-3模型相较随机猜测平均提升了近20个百分点，但距离专家级准确率仍需大幅改进[9]。

随着模型规模扩大，研究重心逐渐从显式知识提取转向复杂结构化推理。尽管有观点认为扩展规模即可全面隐式编码常识，但评测表明，先进神经模型在表达涉及复杂关系的隐式常识时依然面临困难[7]。例如在少样本设定下，175B参数的GPT-3模型的表现比在特定常识图谱上训练的小模型仍低约12个绝对百分点[7]。同时，针对模型“推理”能力的评测也迎来了方法论的反思。早期推理基准被批评过于简单，无法支撑关于模型具备真实推理能力的夸大主张[49]。由于语言模型本质上提供最可能的文本补全而缺乏逻辑保证，研究者引入目标导向的确定性规划框架，以测量模型在行动与状态变化上的真实边界[49]。在算法推理等需要多步生成的场景中，单次生成的成功率随代码模块增加呈指数级下降，这也促使评测框架引入自然语言分层约束，以测试模型在组合验证空间下的代码合成能力[48]。

在多语言与语言学特征演进方面，早期依赖机器翻译英语基准来构建多语言评测的做法，暴露出引入翻译伪影及无法捕捉特定社会文化特征的缺陷，促使了基于原生语料从头构建基准的转向[21]。对于具丰富形态句法的语言，传统语义测试亦显不足。层级探测（probing）分支研究发现，高度多语言模型能在中间网络层定位句法知识，而部分专注特定语系训练的模型却未能有效捕获此类句法特征[25]。从宏观任务精度到微观神经表示的演进，构成了当前大模型度量技术的重要前史。

sections.title: 评价对象、威胁模型与测量
sections.body:
语言模型能力评测的演进深刻反映了其底层机制与应用场景的变迁。在评价对象的早期阶段，模型评测主要关注特定应用中的领域适应能力。当时的测量机制侧重于应对训练与测试数据之间的分布不匹配（domain mismatch）以及由罕见词导致的数据稀疏性问题，往往通过结合自动数据选择与循环神经网络语言模型（RNNLM）的特征来提升泛化性能，其评估高度依赖于特定领域的统计测度[3]。

随着大型语言模型被应用于大规模代码合成等复杂推理任务，评价对象从单纯的文本概率预测转向对高阶规范和复杂逻辑执行能力的综合考量。这一转变直接催生了多维度的威胁模型框架。针对以Codex为代表的代码生成模型，早期的危险分析不仅审视其生成能力，更强调其在处理无正式规范和不可靠训练数据时的局限性[27]。在具体的测量机制上，此类框架深入探究了模型能力的边界。例如，尽管模型能够处理少量变量的关联，但当提示词中涉及四个或更多变量的相互依赖关系时，若相关逻辑未在训练数据中高频出现，Codex等模型的推理能力便会发生显著衰退[27]。为了应对这种深层逻辑隐患，威胁模型甚至向底层机制延伸，建议将模型的API输出直接与编程语言的抽象语法树（AST）对齐，以更稳健地适配现有的安全审计探测机制[27]。

在代码生成领域，相较于单纯验证模型自身输出的静态分析（即“自动驾驶”模式），现代测量机制逐步分化出以人类开发者真实交互为核心的实证评估分支。针对大模型可能直接建议网络安全漏洞的担忧，基于用户对照研究的动态测量机制提供了有别于基准刷榜的视角。通过在内存安全缺陷极易触发的底层语言（如C语言）环境中设置链表开发任务，实验测量表明，引入大模型辅助开发并不会直接引发显著的安全危机——模型辅助组产生严重安全漏洞的比例相比无辅助控制组增幅不超过10%[52]。然而，这种结合用户行为的测量方式也揭示了隐蔽的交互性风险：开发者常常利用AI模型带来的生产力提升来加速编码，却未能有效识别并修复模型建议中本身夹带的代码缺陷；即使他们对建议代码的变量名等进行了微调，底层的逻辑漏洞依然被无意识地保留并部署[52]。

此外，广义的威胁模型与评测对象已经突破了代码能否安全执行的单一维度，开始拓展至知识归属与合规性边界的探测。研究指出，模型生成的代码在解决常规编程问题时，能够有效绕过诸如MOSS等传统代码反抄袭软件的检测[52]。这一现象不仅揭示了评测机制面临的新挑战，也进一步证明了对语言模型能力的评价必须从早期的统计精度测量，走向涵盖人机信任、逻辑边界探测以及交互安全性的全域综合验证。

sections.title: 基准构建、检测与防护
sections.body:
语言模型能力评测的演进不仅体现在任务难度的增加，更核心的在于基准构建机制的结构性转变。早期阶段的语言模型评估往往采用扁平化（Flat）的数据集导向框架，即将常用数据集松散组合，并普遍依赖过度简化的评分策略——直接对跨数据集的独立指标进行简单平均。这种机制严重忽略了不同自然语言处理任务间的异质性与度量差异，导致最终的单一均分无法准确反映模型在特定语言能力层面（如推理或生成）的真实优劣，破坏了基准作为通用语言智能指示器的可靠性。

为解决上述系统性缺失，现代基准构建机制开始向自顶向下的层次化（Hierarchical）框架发生范式转移。以中文语言理解与生成评测基准CUGE为例，其摒弃了传统的底层数据堆砌模式，创新性地构建了“能力-任务-数据集”的三级分类体系[19]。在这种机制下，基准设计参考人类语言考试大纲，将通用语言智能预先解构为篇章级理解、信息获取与问答、多语言及数学推理等七大核心能力，随后再向下映射至代表性任务和具体数据集。这种结构化设计的核心优势在于其支持多级评分策略（Multi-level scoring strategy），使得研究者能够基于层次框架输出不同细粒度的模型性能评估结果，从而精细化定位语言模型在特定能力层级的真实表现与提升空间[19]。

在通用自然语言基准之外，面向特定下游模态的语言模型评测则展现出差异化的机制侧重点。尤其是在自动语音识别（ASR）领域，语言模型的评测焦点从静态文本的完形填空，显著转向对动态、长跨度词史（word history）信息的连续映射能力评估。例如，在针对递回式神经网络语言模型（RNNLM）的评测中，研究者通常以大词汇量连续语音识别（LVCSR）任务作为核心的实证检验基准[2]。在该特定任务基准下，评测机制重点考察模型在结合词史相关额外信息线索时，通过递归方式捕获长距离词汇规律的有效性，以及利用动态模型估计方法获取特定话语（utterance-specific）特征的性能表现[2]。这种依托LVCSR任务开展的纵深对比评测，构成了对通用层次化基准不可或缺的专业补充。

需要特别指出的是，全面而可靠的语言模型评测应当涵盖对恶意注入、数据投毒等威胁的检测与防护机制。然而，基于严谨的文献适用范围，当前有效材料集中于基础评测框架的架构演进与特定任务的性能检验，尚未涵盖针对语言模型幻觉甄别、对抗鲁棒性检测或对齐防护策略的具体技术论证。因此，关于安全检测与防护维度的机制探讨予以明确限定，暂不涉及相关无证据主张。

sections.title: 有效性、鲁棒性和外推边界
sections.body:
语言模型能力的评测正逐步从常规的同分布任务，向低资源场景、复杂语义现象等边缘地带延伸，以全面探究模型的有效性、鲁棒性及其外推边界。在评测方法的分支演进中，针对跨分布和隐含语义偏移的测量机制尤为关键。

在鲁棒性与外推边界的评测分支中，多语言及语码交替（Code-Switching）场景构成了重要的测试床。传统的语言模型在面对多语言混合输入时，常受限于真实混合数据的稀缺以及语言间语法结构的错位。为了探明模型在此类数据不平衡条件下的外推能力，研究者改变了直接依赖真实数据的评测范式。例如，基于等价约束（Equivalence Constraint）理论，通过形态素分割与词对齐技术，人工合成合乎语法的混合语言文本进行模型增强与评估[36]。这种机制转变允许在无额外真实混合语音数据的条件下，验证语言模型处理复杂输入形态的鲁棒性。在有效性测量上，此类方法不仅通过困惑度（如实现29-34%的相对增益）等客观指标来量化模型的边界扩展，还结合人类主观判断评估生成数据与真实生态数据的接近度，以此确立外推分布的可靠性[36]。

在语义理解的有效性探测分支中，模型处理选择性限制（Selectional Restrictions）违背现象（如逻辑转喻中的论元强制）的能力是评估其语义推理边界的核心指标。传统方法在无监督地捕捉这种隐含意图时面临挑战。为了评测和提升模型对论元强制（Argument Coercion）的检测能力，评测机制演进为通过无监督主题模型（如带有谓词归纳和选择类变量的cLDA）来进行概率推断[1]。与依赖单一显式特征不同，该机制利用谓词-类别与论元-类别的概率混合，对谓词-论元对进行连续区间打分（低分指向强制现象），从而在不依赖标注数据的情况下，评估模型识别非标准语义搭配的有效性[1]。这种基于数据分布采样的打分机制，揭示了模型在面对单义常见谓词与多义词汇时，无监督语义归纳能力的边界差异。

综上，针对模型有效性和鲁棒性的评测，正从单一的性能跑分转向对模型内在机制的深层探测。无论是通过语法理论约束生成跨语言外推数据，还是利用无监督概率模型检测深层语义违背现象，这些演进机制均极大地丰富了对语言模型在极端或复杂约束下能力边界的认知。

sections.title: 实验证据与方法比较
sections.body:
语言模型评测逐渐暴露出现有指标的局限与冲突。传统的困惑度和全局准确率极易受齐夫分布影响，导致低频词惩罚，掩盖模型在开放域生成中的实际语义可用性[6][22]。然而，当训练数据限定在人类发展合理规模时，困惑度能有效反映模型与人类神经行为的对齐程度[29]，甚至可作为下游代码任务的低成本评估代理[28]。为避免复杂任务军备竞赛，评估演进出针对琐碎任务的自动单元测试[44]；早期依赖单一语料规模的基准[4]开始向细粒度对照诊断转型。

评测范式从端到端打分转向施加严密的对照条件。结构知识检验利用最小对立体探测局部约束与C-统御[5]，将心理语言学实验平台化以验证句法机制[12]，或通过句法启动效应分离语义与抽象结构表征[23]。评测还通过疑问化反事实条件句限制推理捷径[18]，系统隔离36类语言现象以暴露推断缺陷[38]。在约束生成方面，评估引入基于正则表达式状态机的大规模形式化验证[57]，以及利用上下文无关文法限制解码空间的语义解析测试[31]。针对纯文本分布伪影，评测扩展至棋类等闭域环境，利用完整状态追踪机制消除不可观测干扰[26]；代码理解中则通过对齐抽象语法树的注意力权重，暴露了模型不及位置偏移基线的结构弱点[32]。

任务构建呈现难度分级与语言类型学分化。生成任务被拆分为多级难度以量化泛化边界[8]。多语言评测从早期从头构建原生语料基准[11]、防过拟合未公开数据校验[56]及专属生成框架[30]，向深层特性扩展：如西班牙语评估涵盖了基于语篇连贯的序列特征[42]。类型学测试揭示了深层差异：日语测试暴露出模型对语序和格助词极不敏感[37]；英西对比表明模型的句法偏好往往源于非语言近因偏差，而非通用规律[10]。此外，基于类型学特征的预测机制能替代翻译，更无偏地估计零样本迁移[34]；中低资源场景下单语定制模型常优于大规模多语言架构[17]，但在特定推理中，高资源语言思维链中间步骤却能反向提升低资源语言解题率[45]。研究还通过声形感知嵌入探测正字法差异[43]，利用伪概率评估无监督语音建模[13]，而跨文化评测更揭示了摆脱西方中心化偏见的深刻挑战[59]。

实验揭示了架构在各类场景下的机制盲点与脆弱性。零样本泛化中，自回归因果解码器表现最佳，但掩码模型结合多任务微调亦能在特定对齐下反超[58]；常识评测表明零样本的高性能往往源于数据集偏差[14]，但大规模模型在物理属性判断中却展现出克服局部共现报告偏差的能力[39]。指令微调无法填补模型在语用学会话含义推理上的鸿沟[54]；定向微调虽能唤醒被掩盖的隐式语言知识[24]，但在事实一致性评测中，解码器依旧优先给违背事实但字面摘抄文本打高分[41]。代码漏洞修复成功率极度依赖提示注释的句法分布[20]。句法保持替换[40]与对抗性拼写微扰[15]分别暴露出模型在维持语言结构稳定性和保持语义鲁棒性方面的深层缺陷。对话问答中，将历史线索直接作为文本提示注入比修改特征表征更具鲁棒性[47]；困难推理任务中，仅依赖答案评分会严重低估能力，必须结合思维链反映真实计算边界[35]。最后，语音理解应用中，紧凑模型在维持可比错误率的同时显著降低了部署生态影响，但这取决于具体的压缩方法，且特定模型效果甚至优于蒸馏版本[33]。

sections.title: 局限、效率与开放问题
sections.body:
尽管语言模型在各项基准上取得了显著成绩，但现有的评测方法在适用条件、测量有效性及部署成本上仍面临严峻局限。首先，在评测指标的有效性与泛化边界检测方面，基础指标与实际能力之间存在机制性脱节。验证集的预训练损失（如困惑度）无法完全解释模型在下游任务中的表现差异；研究发现，即使预训练损失相同，不同参数配置的模型也会因优化算法（如带小批量噪声的随机梯度下降）对平缓极小值的隐式偏好，而导致下游任务的迁移能力大相径庭[51]。同时，由于模型倾向于拟合容易学习的表层文本相关性而非深层语义逻辑，其在分布外（OOD）数据上的鲁棒性往往大幅下降[46]。这引发了研究界对模型是否真正具备“理解”能力的争议：许多自然语言理解基准（如GLUE）的高分表现，可能仅仅是模型利用了数据的脆弱启发式特征，而非实现了类似人类的认知推理[55]。为了在无标注目标域数据时估计这种分布偏移，虽然引入了基于隐层属性的无监督泛化度量，但其与实际分布外准确率的等级相关性依然受限[46]。

其次，在特定维度的风险测量机制上，当前方法表现出极大的脆弱性。以社会偏见量化为例，广泛使用的模板化填空评测机制极不可靠；在保持语义不变的前提下对模板进行人工微调，会导致特定任务（如自然语言推断或掩码语言建模）的偏见测量结果发生剧烈波动，这种不稳定性证明单一静态模板难以真实反映模型的复杂行为模式，容易产生误导性结论[50]。

最后，评测体系的适用边界还受到计算成本与语言多样性的制约。大规模语言模型的极高计算开销严重限制了其推理部署，促使研究转向渐进式非结构化幅度剪枝等压缩技术，以在仅保留约十分之一参数量的条件下，维持通用模型在特定（如生物医学）领域的跨域迁移质量[53]。此外，在多语言评测场景中，通用的统一文本框架（如mT5）在面对具有丰富方言变体和复杂形态的低资源语言时，其跨语言迁移能力存在明显瓶颈；针对特定语言族群进行专门的序列预训练（如AraT5），成为突破通用架构能力盲区、触及生成与理解评测上限的必要条件[16]。
